data.gender_notes: Linga is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Linga represents the divine phallus of Lord Shiva. It is a symbol of creation, fertility, and regeneration. The name Linga carries the meaning “Symbol of Shiva” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Linga usually hope their child will grow to embody symbol of shiva and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace the divine masculine energy and creative potential.
data.etymology: Linga belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Symbol of Shiva.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Linga total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The Lingam is one of the most revered symbols in Hinduism, especially in Shaivism, dedicated to Lord Shiva. This symbol is integral to Shiva temples, and it is believed that circumambulating or worshiping a Lingam can invoke the blessings of Lord Shiva.
data.spiritual_significance: For Hindus, the Lingam signifies the inner self or the soul. By focusing on the Lingam during prayers, devotees consecrate their inner selves to the divine. According to Hindu text, the cosmic conscious energy lies within it. Thus, the worship of the Lingam is a way to attain self-realization and spiritual enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The symbol Linga represents the divine phallic form of Shiva, embodying the creative and generative power of the universe. It is a reminder of the divine masculine energy and the cyclical nature of creation and destruction.

historical_references.reference: The Linga Purana, one of the eighteen major Puranas, is an important text in Hinduism that deals with the worship of the Lingam form of Shiva. The text is believed to have been composed between the 7th and 10th centuries CE.

The Linga is also a symbol of Shiva as the creator of the universe, representing the divine male phallus and the creative power of the universe. This concept is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures, including the Agama texts which date back to the 2nd century BCE and the later Puranic texts.
historical_references.context: Symbol of Shiva as creator and divine male phallus
